newsitem.title: UK: Wm Morrison says Q1 sales up 2.1 pct so far.
newsitem.headline: Wm Morrison says Q1 sales up 2.1 pct so far.

text.p: Britain's Wm Morrison Supermarkets said on Thursday that its sales in the first quarter of the current financial year was running 2.1 percent above year-ago period.
Chairman Ken Morrison told the annual meeting that food prices for March falling 1.6 percent according to figures from the British Retail Consortium.
"The absence of price inflation when cost inflation continues poses a challenge for our industry," Morrison said.
Morrison added that the company hoped to have representation of its link-up with Midland Bank "in most stores by the end of the decade."
Morrison said in March that it would link up with Midland, part of HSBC Holdings, to provide banking and financial services to customers in store.

Morrison also told the annual meeting that he "warmly welcomed" the new Labour government's proposals for an independent Food Safety Agency and added that he hoped changes might be made in the planning regime to speed up decisions and give "a more liberal approach."
He confirmed the company's plans to open 11 new superstores with investment of 200 million stg and the creation of over 5,000 jobs.

"I view the future with considerable confidence and optimism. I firmly believe in our ability to prosper in what will undoubtedly continue to be tough times," Morrison said. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
